My name is Freddy Agama. I am from Peru and I studied at the National University of Engineering (UNI). I have my bachelor's degree in Mechatronics Engineering (robotic, industrial automation). My research interests are Control Systems, Process Control & Industrial Automation and Robotics. My dreams are to study and get a master's or Phd degree in a top university such as UofA, TUM or MIT and work for a big company like Nasa, SpaceX, Tesla or Boston Dynamics. After that I would like to run my own company. My hobbies are playing soccer, swimming, piano, and traveling around the world. I am in Canada since January 1st, 2020 and I am currently doing my research internship at CCWJ at the University of Alberta (UofA). I have also studied for one semester at Hochschule Furtwangen University (HFU) in Germany (2018) where I took some courses such as Deep Learning and Internet of Things, and another semester at Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) in Spain (2019) where I took some courses such as Robotics and Industrial Automation. From October 2017 to Septemeber 2018, I was the electronic leader in a research team called Naylamp UNI in my home university. This project focused on designing, constructing and controlling 2 small ships. We competed in the HydroContest 2018 in Saint Tropez, France (http://bit.ly/2ue5Kzq). Spanish is my native language, but I also speak English and basic German. You can download my CV here (http://bit.ly/2SCCziM).

#### Project

Title: Closed-Loop Microcontroller Torch Control In Welding Automation. 

An automated vertical standoff system for a stationary GMAW torch will be designed in this project. This project is intended to improve the weld quality by regulating the current in gas metal arc welding process (GMAW) for this purpose an electro-mechanical system consisting of a linear guide rail and an electric actuator carrying the welding torch should modify the contact tip to workpiece distance (CTWD). The prototype uses a microcontroller in conjunction with sensors to acquire, analyze and control the vertical position of the welding torch in response to geometric changes in the surface of the welding plate that are sensed through the fluctuations in the welding current.

In GMAW, voltage and wire-feed speed are controlled and kept constant. An important factor that translates into a quality weld is to keep the CTWD constant, however due to imperfections in the material’s surface the CTWD changes translating into a change in current due to a direct relationship, creating discrepancies and thus bad quality in the weld. For this purpose, the automated CTWD-Torch control is being developed using a feedback control loop to tackle this perturbances and maintain a set point according to the client’s needs.
